items.definition: Medium-sized river cargo boats of the Ribatejo that sailed between the Tagus towns and Lisbon, carrying goods in both directions.

numbers.what: water depth needed to sail, even in midsummer
minimum voyage time to Lisbon in good weather and fair wind

items.definition: Alternative name for the upriver boats, tying them to the Ribatejo region they served.
Describes the boats' very shallow draught, which let them sail loaded in low water.

numbers.what: water depth sufficient for the voyage

items.definition: The beam, meaning the width of the hull.
The tall mast, strongly raked aft, that carried the boat's large triangular sail.
Describes the mast's backward rake toward the stern.
The name of the large triangular main sail set on the mast.
A small sail set at the bow, in addition to the main sail.
The skipper, who could be the owner, commanded the boat and steered at the helm.
The helm or rudder, operated by the arrais to steer the boat.
Experienced seamen forming the working crew aboard the boat.
Young crew members aboard to learn the trade and secure the future of navigation.
Upriver. These boats were only permitted to sail in the calm river, not at sea beyond the bar.
The river mouth bar, beyond which the upriver boats were not allowed to sail.
A favourable, fair wind that, with good weather, made the voyage to Lisbon possible in about two days.
To lower or take in the sail, used figuratively for the boats ceasing to operate.
To come alongside or berth at a quay or bank.
River landing places where goods were gathered for loading and unloaded on arrival, such as Abrantes, Constância and Chamusca.
Silting of the riverbed, which reduced navigability once dams and lower water flow came.
The undammed Tagus, with abundant freely flowing water, which allowed larger boats to travel far upriver.
A traditional Tagus sailing boat, now used for leisure trips on the river.

title: mediotejo, Portos do Tejo e barcos d'água acima
